description:
We’re a team of engineering and mathematics students passionate about problem-solving, innovation, and tackling real-world challenges. 

We’re looking for motivated teammates with skills in coding, mathematical modeling, CAD, data analysis, or design. Let’s build something awesome together!
summary:
We developed Parched Planet, an interactive web application that uses 25 years of NASA Earth science data to identify environmental trends and determine whether they are statistically significant. Users can select environmental variables, explore changes over time, and compare two distinct regions: South Florida and Arizona.

Our tool addresses the challenge by simplifying access to and analysis of NASA datasets, including GPM IMERG, GLDAS, MERRA-2, and MODIS. Rather than requiring users to navigate thousands of variables or possess statistical expertise, Parched Planet automates data preparation and applies the Mann-Kendall test, Sen’s slope, and t-tests to identify meaningful trends while accounting for autocorrelation. It then translates complex statistical results into clear, accessible conclusions.

This matters because floods, droughts, and rising temperatures threaten communities, agriculture, and water resources. Our findings reveal that although rainfall shows no significant trend in either region, vapor pressure deficit is increasing significantly, indicating that the atmosphere is becoming increasingly capable of extracting moisture from soil and vegetation. By making NASA data accessible to everyone, Parched Planet empowers residents, educators, planners, and decision-makers to better understand the environmental changes affecting their communities.
details:
Parched Planet allows users to explore environmental changes through interactive visualizations, regional comparisons, and statistical explanations. Users can investigate different environmental variables, examine historical trends, and explore how factors such as temperature and water availability influence atmospheric drying.

The application makes complex scientific information easier to understand without requiring users to interpret raw datasets or perform statistical calculations themselves. It also demonstrates how observation periods and regional differences can influence scientific conclusions.

We intend for Parched Planet to become an accessible educational and research resource that helps communities better understand their changing environments. Ultimately, we hope to encourage informed decisions regarding water management, environmental planning, and climate resilience.

We developed the application using R and Shiny, creating an interactive, browser-based platform. We incorporated publicly available NASA Earth science datasets and used statistical methods to analyze and visualize environmental trends. No specialized hardware was required.

Our project combines scientific analysis with an imaginative Pizza Planet concept. This contrast between an imaginary planet and Earth reinforces our central message: understanding our planet requires real observations and scientific evidence. We also transform complex statistical findings into accessible visualizations and explanations.

We considered accessibility, data reliability, regional differences, seasonal variability, record length, and statistical accuracy. We also prioritized making the application intuitive for users without scientific or programming backgrounds.
